top_stories.title: Bitcoin holds ~$65K as ETF inflows hit best week since April and the Senate stalls on the Clarity Act
points: Bitcoin traded around $64,910–$65,200, up about 3.7% for the week, after failing to decisively break $65K.

US spot Bitcoin ETFs (funds that hold actual BTC and trade on a stock exchange, giving investors exposure without managing wallets) drew $754.69M over the week — the strongest pace since April — including $853M over the weekend alone, with BlackRock's IBIT taking the majority.
The Senate failed to reach the 60 votes needed for the Clarity Act (a proposed US framework defining how cryptocurrencies are regulated), pushing any action to September 14.

The delay was largely priced in, so the bid is coming from flows and macro rather than Washington: a weak July jobs report softened the dollar, easing pressure on dollar-denominated assets like Bitcoin.

Hedge funds turned net long on CME Bitcoin futures (regulated contracts to buy/sell BTC at a future date) for the first time in months, signaling professional traders betting on upside rather than shorting.
Bitcoin whales (holders of 10,000+ BTC) and 'sharks' (10–10,000 BTC) accumulated over 20,000 BTC (~$1.2B) in a single week despite the flat price.

unique_angles.point: Frames the inflow week as broad 'crypto ETF' strength (not just Bitcoin), read as institutional sentiment turning positive after a stretch of caution.

Analysts call the remaining flows 'more tactical than convicted'; the Coldcard hardware wallet hack ($120M loss, July 30) plus the CLARITY Act delay are suppressing institutional appetite, while Santiment data points to a possible $70K+ target if BTC closes decisively above $65K.
Reads the Senate failure as confirmation rather than a fresh shock, with over $500M of August ETF inflows still landing on consecutive days.

items.title: BIP-110 fork dies in two blocks as miners follow the money
points: BIP-110, a proposal to restrict Ordinals inscriptions (non-financial data such as images stored inside Bitcoin transactions), failed to win developer consensus.
Supporters forked the chain (split off a competing version of Bitcoin with different rules) at block 961,632 and it survived only two blocks.

The fork inherited Bitcoin's full mining difficulty (the amount of computational work required to produce a valid block) but attracted only a fraction of hashpower (total processing capacity), making it unprofitable, so miners returned to the original chain.
No regulator or central authority intervened — economic incentives alone resolved the dispute, validating Bitcoin's decentralized governance premise.

items.title: Coinsbuy loses $8M in coordinated cross-chain attack
points: On August 9 an attacker drained 6.04M USDT from eight TRON wallets plus 1.89M USDT and 77 ETH from three Ethereum wallets.
The vector appears to be a withdrawal-path flaw rather than stolen private keys (the secret cryptographic codes controlling assets), since Coinsbuy refilled the drained wallets within 24 hours.
79% of stolen funds were routed through instant exchange FixedFloat via ~50 single-use addresses to obscure the trail; ~$542,000 in ETH sits unmoved across five addresses.
2026 industry hack losses now total $972 million year-to-date.

items.title: Mastercard buys stablecoin firm BVNK for $1.8B
points: The acquisition deepens major payment networks' integration of stablecoins (tokens pegged 1:1 to a currency like the US dollar).
Separately, Robinhood launched zero-fee crypto trading in the UK.

items.title: Ether.fi exits EigenLayer as liquid restaking collapses
points: Ether.fi moved restaking exposure out of its weETH token into a separate Symbiotic-based weETHs token, cutting restaking exposure in weETH to under 1% (restaking = reusing staked ETH to secure additional networks for extra yield).

EigenLayer total value locked (TVL, the dollar value of assets deposited in a protocol) fell from $22.06B to $5.10B; the whole liquid restaking sector shrank from an $18.3B December 2024 peak to under $5B as venture-funded incentives ended.
Ether.fi's own TVL dropped from a $12.43B August 2025 peak to $3.3B; ETHFI fell 11.4% on the week and EIGEN is down 20.8% on the month.
Full EigenPod withdrawal-credential removal is planned for Q4 2026, completing the exit; EigenLayer's CEO called it the 'end of an era' and blamed a premature launch.

items.title: Helius launches Rings privacy layer on Solana
points: A permissionless 'public ring' tier hides transaction amounts while revealing sender and recipient, blocking amount-based MEV extraction (profit taken by reordering or front-running pending transactions).
A permissioned, customizable tier conceals sender, recipient and amounts, aimed at institutions and neobanks needing configurable compliance controls.
Both tiers run on existing Solana infrastructure, requiring no new chain or consensus changes; DeFi integrations for staking, trading and lending are planned.

items.title: HALO launches decentralized AI inference network on Base
points: A permissionless marketplace for AI model inference (running a trained model to produce answers) settles payments in USDC on Base mainnet with no geographic restrictions or accounts.

Verification uses SPEX (Statistical Proof of Execution): outputs are fingerprinted as Bloom filters (compact data structures for membership checks) and probed by independent verifiers — honest runs almost fully overlap the fingerprint while fraudulent ones drop to the false-positive floor, avoiding trusted hardware or zero-knowledge proofs.
Token emissions follow a fixed declining schedule tied to verified usage, protocol fees fund programmatic buybacks into the treasury, and zero supply is reserved for venture investors.
Session keys abstract gas fees and per-transaction signing while keeping self-custody; one centralized routing layer remains until federation to staked relayers ships in H2 2026.

items.title: Crypto consolidation leaves four sectors with product-market fit
points: Only memecoins, perpetuals, yield and prediction markets are seen as having durable demand.
Non-financial protocols face effective extinction unless they return capital by Q1 2027.

sections.title: BIP-110 Fork: How Bitcoin's Market Mechanism Rejected a Proposal
points: Proposal to restrict Ordinals inscriptions (non-financial data stored on blockchain) failed to achieve consensus in the developer community.
BIP-110 supporters forked the blockchain at block 961,632 to implement their preferred rules, exercising their right to create an alternate chain.

Miners, acting on pure economic incentive, abandoned the fork after two blocks because the original Bitcoin chain was more profitable—the fork had inherited full mining difficulty (computational work required to validate blocks) but attracted only a fraction of hashpower (processing capacity).
No central authority intervened; market forces resolved the dispute, confirming Bitcoin's design premise that economic incentives guide decentralized consensus without top-down control.

Weak July jobs report softened the U.S. dollar, reducing headwinds for dollar-denominated commodities like Bitcoin; hedge funds on CME futures turned net long for the first time in months, indicating professional traders are increasingly betting on price appreciation.

sections.title: Coinsbuy $8 Million Hack Highlights Cross-Chain Vulnerability
points: Attacker drained 6.04 million USDT from eight TRON wallets and 1.89 million USDT plus 77 ETH from three Ethereum wallets in a coordinated operation on August 9.

Attacker routed 79% of stolen funds through instant exchange FixedFloat using approximately 50 single-use addresses to obscure the trail; approximately $542,000 in ETH remains unmoved across five addresses.
